 LA.APP. NO. 176 OF 2022  3  2025:KER:73466  JUDGMENT 1.

The State Government has filed this Land Acquisition Appeal under Section 74 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the LA Act, 2013').

sentences.text: 2. This Appeal arises from the Land Acquisition Reference disposed of by the Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority, Alappuzha (hereinafter referred to as 'the Reference Authority') by an Award dated 13.01.2020.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority, Alappuzha
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3. The State Government initiated land acquisition proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the LA Act, 1894') to acquire 21.580 hectares of land spread in 9 villages, namely, Karumadi, Karuvatta, Cheruthana, Haripad, Thakazhi South, Thakazhi North,
Kumarapuram, Ambalappuzha and Veeyapuram in Karthikappally,
LA.APP
. NO. 176 OF 2022 2025:KER:73466 Ambalappuzha and Kuttanad Taluks for doubling the railway track between Haripad and Ambalappuzha.
Later, the total extent of land required for acquisition was reduced to 19.24.33 Hectares.
The land involved in the present Reference is dry land in category No.A and wet land in category No.A situated in Karuvatta village.

The description of category No.A with respect to dry land is 'dry land with tar road access' and category No.A with respect to wet land is 'wet land State Of Kerala vs *Muraleedharan Pillai on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139077320/
2 with pathway access'.
4. Section 4(1) Notification under the LA Act, 1894 is dated 24.06.2010.

When the LA Act, 2013 came into force with effect from 01.01.2014, on the direction of the Government, the Land Acquisition Officer passed a temporary Award, fixing the land value @ Rs.77,880/- per Are for dry land and @ Rs.6,000/- per Are for wet land, as the Rules under LA Act, 2013 were not framed.

After framing the Rules, the Land Acquisition Officer passed the final Award fixing land value @
Rs.80,420/- per Are for dry land and @ Rs.7,566/- per Are for wet land.
The District Level Purchase Committee (DLPC) had fixed the market value of the land after conducting a detailed negotiation with landowners.

The DLPC had fixed the land value @
Rs.2,59,455/- per Are for dry land and @ Rs.19,768/- per Are for wet land.
The formula adopted by DLPC was to take 200% of the basic land value with 30% solatium and 12% additional land value [Basic Land value + 30% Solatium +12% Addl Land Value) X 200%].
The market value fixed by the DLPC was approved by the State Level Empowered Committee (SLEC).
Several landowners settled their claims by accepting the market value fixed by the DLPC.

6. The Reference Authority awarded enhanced compensation fixing the land value @ Rs.2,33,640/-
per Are for dry land and @ Rs.18,000/- per Are for wet land.

The Reference Authority fixed the land value relying on the basic land value fixed by the DLPC and fixed market value, adding 200% of the basic land value to the basic land value [Basic Land Value + 200% of Basic Land Value].

In effect,
300% of the basic land value of LA.APP. NO. 176 OF 2022 2025:KER:73466 Rs.77,880/- per Are for dry land and Rs.6,000/- per Are for wet land fixed by the DLPC was taken to arrive at the market value of Rs.2,33,640/- per Are for dry land and Rs.18,000/- per Are for wet land fixed by the Reference Authority.

7. In the judgment dated 02.07.2025 in L.A. Appeal No.252/2021 & connected cases arising from the very same Section 4(1) Notification, this Court has found that there is no rationale to add 200%
to the basic land value by the Reference Court instead of 100% added by the DLPC and that such an addition of 200% by the Reference Authority is arbitrary and without any material to support the same and accordingly fixed land value by taking 200% of the Basic Land Value fixed by DLPC.
The same criterion is applicable in this appeal also.

8. In this case, DLPC had fixed the Basic Land Value at Rs.77,880/-
per Are for dry land and 200% of the same is Rs.1,55,760/- per Are and Rs.6,000/- per Are for wet land and 200% of the same is Rs.12,000/- per Are.

9. Accordingly, this Appeal is allowed in part without costs, LA.APP. NO. 176 OF 2022 2025:KER:73466 modifying the impugned Award so far as it relates to the fixation of market value of the land, by fixing land value @ Rs.1,55,760/- per Are for dry land and @ Rs.12,000/- per Are for wet land for the acquired land instead of Rs.2,33,640/- per Are for dry land and Rs.18,000/- per Are for wet land fixed by the Reference Authority.

The impugned award in all other respects is State Of Kerala vs *Muraleedharan Pillai on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139077320/
3 confirmed.

M.A.ABDUL HAKHIM JUDGE Shg/
